# DIAL

> Dynamic Integration between AI and Labor

This file contains links to documentation sections following the llmstxt.org standard.

## Table of Contents

- [AI Agent Experience](https://eloquentanalytics.github.io/dialai/docs/agent-experience): DIAL is designed for LLM-driven agents to participate as proposers and voters in decision cycles, to design state machines that encode governance w...
- [CLI Reference](https://eloquentanalytics.github.io/dialai/docs/api/cli): The `dialai` command-line interface runs state machines to completion.
- [`createSession(machine: MachineDefinition): Promise<Session>`](https://eloquentanalytics.github.io/dialai/docs/api/createSession): Creates a new session instance from a machine definition. Generates a UUID, sets `currentState` to `machine.initialState`, and stores the session.
- [`evaluateConsensus(sessionId): Promise<ConsensusResult>`](https://eloquentanalytics.github.io/dialai/docs/api/evaluateConsensus): Evaluates whether consensus has been reached for a session without executing any transition. This is a read-only operation that checks the current ...
- [`executeTransition(sessionId, transitionName, toState, reasoning?): Promise<Session>`](https://eloquentanalytics.github.io/dialai/docs/api/executeTransition): Executes a state transition on a session. Validates the transition is valid from the current state, records it in history, updates `currentState`, ...
- [`getSession(sessionId: string): Promise<Session>`](https://eloquentanalytics.github.io/dialai/docs/api/getSession): Retrieves a session by its ID. Returns the full session object including current state, history, and machine definition.
- [`getSessions(): Promise<Session[]>`](https://eloquentanalytics.github.io/dialai/docs/api/getSessions): Returns all stored sessions. Useful for listing active sessions or debugging.
- [API Reference](https://eloquentanalytics.github.io/dialai/docs/api/intro): The `dialai` library provides functions for creating sessions, registering specialists, and managing the decision cycle. For the conceptual foundat...
- [`registerArbiter(opts): Promise<Arbiter>`](https://eloquentanalytics.github.io/dialai/docs/api/registerArbiter): Registers an arbiter specialist for a machine. Arbiters evaluate consensus among proposals and determine winning transitions.
- [`registerProposer(opts): Promise<Proposer>`](https://eloquentanalytics.github.io/dialai/docs/api/registerProposer): Registers a proposer specialist for a machine. Proposers submit state transition proposals during the decision cycle.
- [`registerVoter(opts): Promise<Voter>`](https://eloquentanalytics.github.io/dialai/docs/api/registerVoter): Registers a voter specialist for a machine. Voters compare proposals pairwise and vote for their preferred option.
- [`runSession(machine: MachineDefinition): Promise<Session>`](https://eloquentanalytics.github.io/dialai/docs/api/runSession): Runs a machine to completion. Creates a session, registers specialists (from the machine definition or a built-in deterministic proposer), and loop...
- [`submitArbitration(sessionId, roundId?, specialistId?, transitionName?, reasoning?, metaJson?, costUSD?, latencyMsec?, numInputTokens?, numOutputTokens?): Promise<ArbitrationResult>`](https://eloquentanalytics.github.io/dialai/docs/api/submitArbitration): Evaluates consensus and optionally executes the winning transition. Follows the same unified pattern as `submitProposal` and `submitVote`: if the k...
- [Types Reference](https://eloquentanalytics.github.io/dialai/docs/api/types): Complete type definitions for the `dialai` library. All types are exported from the main package.
- [Alignment Measurement vs. Voting](https://eloquentanalytics.github.io/dialai/docs/concepts/alignment-vs-voting): When building LangChain graphs with multiple models, you face a fundamental question: **Do you need voting, or can you rely solely on direct alignm...
- [Arbitration](https://eloquentanalytics.github.io/dialai/docs/concepts/arbitration): **Arbitration** is the continuous process of evaluating consensus after every proposal and vote to determine when sufficient support exists to exec...
- [Consensus Strategies](https://eloquentanalytics.github.io/dialai/docs/concepts/consensus-strategies): DIAL provides three built-in consensus strategies for arbiters. Each strategy determines when consensus has been reached and which proposal wins. S...
- [Decision Cycle](https://eloquentanalytics.github.io/dialai/docs/concepts/decision-cycle): When a session is not in its goal state, the system progresses through a repeating cycle until it reaches the goal.
- [Human Primacy](https://eloquentanalytics.github.io/dialai/docs/concepts/human-primacy): **The human is always right**, not because humans are infallible, but because humans have context that AI cannot access.
- [Core Concepts](https://eloquentanalytics.github.io/dialai/docs/concepts/intro): DIAL provides a structured approach to AI-human collaboration built around a few key abstractions. This section explains the conceptual foundations...
- [Related Work](https://eloquentanalytics.github.io/dialai/docs/concepts/related-work): DIAL solves a different problem than most AI frameworks. Understanding the distinction helps clarify what DIAL is, and what it isn't.
- [Sessions](https://eloquentanalytics.github.io/dialai/docs/concepts/sessions): A **session** is an instance of a state machine that specialists navigate through decision cycles.
- [Specialists](https://eloquentanalytics.github.io/dialai/docs/concepts/specialists): Specialists are the pluggable actors that participate in sessions. They can be AI models or humans.
